title: Read HN twice a day for the last decade. Here's my list of S-Tier HN links
author: vivzkestrel
raw_text: - Everyday I read 2 pages of HN in the morning and 2 in the evening for years now- Of late, I noticed that most of the stuff on the 1st 2 pages is AI this, AI that, LLM this, LLM that, model here, model there- Today I am going to attempt to break that trend by sharing the greatest resources on HN from my collection of 50000+ bookmarks over the last decade- I have a process on my end for bookmarking- The most visual explainers get S-Tier ranking- Good info from reputed sources gets an A, non reputed gets B- Opinion blogs are at the bottom of the barrel and maybe ranked C, D, E and even F depending on quality- Here's my S-Tier list- Animated explanation of how transformers work https://poloclub.github.io/transformer-explainer/- Visual intro to K-means clustering algorithm https://k-means-explorable.vercel.app/- Animated 3D intro to vision LLMs https://blog.mdturp.ch/posts/2024-04-05-visual_guide_to_vision_transformer.html- Animated intro to machine learning https://r2d3.us/visual-intro-to-machine-learning-part-1/- Animated intro to probability in math https://seeing-theory.brown.edu/basic-probability/index.html- Building a 3D world from scratch in step by step animated manner https://aibodh.com/posts/bevy-tutorial-build-your-first-3d-editor-in-rust/- Visualize algorithms https://algorithm-visualizer.org/- Animated step by step sequence of how a request goes from your browser to the server https://200ms.thenodebook.com/#act-1-the-click- Visual intro to the inner workings of a combustion engine https://ciechanow.ski/internal-combustion-engine/- 3D real time robotics code simulator https://bittlex-sim.petoi.com/- Animated explainer: Elliptic curve cryptography https://growingswe.com/blog/elliptic-curve-cryptography- Rate limiting algorithms visualized https://smudge.ai/blog/ratelimit-algorithms- Visual intro to the graphics pipeline! https://fremaconsulting.ch/blog/vulkan- Animated explanation of how to build ReactJS from scratch! https://pomb.us/build-your-own-react/- Mini game: How to build an entire CPU starting from a basic gate https://select.supply/game/chipbuilder- Assemble a neural network from scratch https://graphgame.sabrina.dev/- 3D visualization: how gravity works https://qunabu.github.io/Gravity/#what-is-gravity- Mini game: how css grid works https://cssgridgarden.com/- Animated math book for linear algebra, vectors etc https://immersivemath.com/ila/index.html- Animated explainer: How FAISS vector search works https://fremaconsulting.ch/blog/faiss- 3D animation of how to build a health wearable from scratch https://www.lumafield.com/scan-of-the-month/health-wearables- 3D animation of how semiconductor manufacturing works https://ig.ft.com/microchips/- Mini game: how git works https://learngitbranching.js.org/- Mini game: SQL from scratch https://sqlpd.com/- Another mini game: SQL https://lost-at-sql.therobinlord.com/- Animated explainers showing how colors, screens, graphics, rendering, shaders, compilers, interpreters work https://www.makingsoftware.com/- Animated explainer shows how networking 7 layer stack works inside out https://fazamhd.com/mental-models/networking/- Animated explainers for linear & logistic regression, neural networks, machine learning https://mlu-explain.github.io/- 3D explanation of collision detection, shaders, rendering, culling and gamedev related stuff https://krupitskas.com/posts/modern_culling_techniques/- 3D animation and explanation of every exercise on the body https://musclewiki.com/- Mini game: build an nvidia gpu from scratch https://jaso1024.com/mvidia/- Animated explanation of forward & back propagation of neural networks https://aegeorge42.github.io/- There are many many many more, I am getting a little tired of typing for today- Anyways enough of those AI opinion posts flooding the front page, take that HN!
summary: this post is a reflection from someone who has consistently read hacker news for a decade. they've observed that the platform is now heavily dominated by ai and llm-related content. to offer a different perspective, they're sharing their personal "s-tier" list of links from their vast collection of bookmarks, specifically highlighting resources that are excellent visual explainers. this is a reminder that while ai and llms are incredibly important right now, there's also immense value in foundational knowledge and other areas of computer science. it encourages you to seek out high-quality, well-explained resources, especially those with strong visuals, to deepen your understanding beyond just the latest trends.
why: it offers curated, visually explained resources to broaden your technical knowledge beyond current ai trends.

title: Ask HN: Dear Anthropic, can we please have thought traces back?
author: exabrial
raw_text: Dear Anthropic, can we please have thought traces back?I can't verify whether or not the LLM is arriving at the conclusion from cheating, or if it's fudging or making stuff up.Opus 4.6 remains the best model because of this.
summary: This discussion highlights the importance of "thought traces" or "chain-of-thought" reasoning in large language models (LLMs). It refers to the ability of an LLM to show its intermediate reasoning steps before arriving at a final answer, rather than just presenting the conclusion. The user is advocating for this feature to be reinstated, emphasizing that it helps in verifying the model's process, ensuring it's not "cheating" or making up information. For you, as you work with LLMs and build agents, transparency and interpretability are vital. Understanding how a model thinks improves debugging, builds trust, and is essential for developing robust and reliable AI systems. When designing your own LLM applications, consider incorporating explicit chain-of-thought prompting to make the model's reasoning clearer.
why: Improves LLM transparency and interpretability, vital for building trustworthy AI agents.

title: Scikit-fingerprints: Python library for scikit-learn compatible molecular fingerprints and chemoinformatics
author: Jakub Adamczyk, Adam Staniszewski
raw_text: We present scikit-fingerprints, a comprehensive, fully scikit-learn compatible library for molecular machine learning in Python, based on RDKit. Molecular fingerprints and related functionalities are workhorses of chemoinformatics, yet the widely used open-source frameworks are not compatible with the wider Python machine learning ecosystem based on scikit-learn conventions. scikit-fingerprints closes this gap, bringing molecular fingerprints, molecular filters, similarity and distance measures, applicability domain estimation, data splitting strategies, and more under a single, familiar interface. Scikit-learn compatibility means that an entire chemoinformatics workflow, from a raw SMILES string to a deployable model, can be assembled from composable building blocks and can reuse the mature tooling of the surrounding ecosystem. The underlying RDKit code makes it familiar and extensible for custom chemoinformatics use cases. We put a strong focus on unified interfaces, ease of use, computational efficiency, customization, and extensibility. scikit-fingerprints makes molecular machine learning faster to prototype, easier to reproduce, and simpler to deploy.
summary: This describes `scikit-fingerprints`, a new Python library designed for chemoinformatics. Specifically, it helps in generating "molecular fingerprints," which are numerical representations of molecules used in machine learning for tasks like drug discovery. The key innovation is its full compatibility with `scikit-learn`, a widely used machine learning library. This compatibility is important because it bridges the gap between specialized scientific domains and general-purpose machine learning tools. For you, this highlights the significance of library compatibility and standardization in data science. It shows how making specialized data and tools accessible within a familiar ML ecosystem can greatly enhance usability and accelerate research across various fields. When you encounter specialized data, think about how you could transform it or find libraries that make it compatible with general-purpose ML tools you already know.
why: Emphasizes library compatibility and standardization, making specialized data accessible for ML.

title: GenAI Added to Google Earth
author: alwa
summary: This news item indicates that generative AI (GenAI) capabilities are being integrated into Google Earth. This means that AI is likely being used to create, enhance, or interact with geographical data in novel ways, perhaps generating realistic landscapes, simulating environments, or providing new interactive experiences based on spatial information. It's a great example of how GenAI extends beyond text or image generation into more complex, real-world applications. For you, this shows the broad applicability of generative AI across different domains and how it can transform user interfaces and data visualization. You could think about how generative AI might be applied to other real-world datasets you encounter, such as sensor data or urban planning information, to create new insights or experiences.
why: Demonstrates real-world GenAI application, transforming spatial data and user experience.

title: GenRec: Towards LLM-Native Recommendation at Netflix
author: Jimmc414
summary: this item points to netflix exploring "llm-native recommendation systems." traditionally, recommendations rely on various filtering methods. an "llm-native" approach suggests leveraging the advanced understanding capabilities of large language models to process user preferences, item descriptions, and contextual information more deeply. this could lead to more nuanced, personalized recommendations or even generate explanations for why certain items are suggested. for you, this is a cutting-edge application of llms and transformers, demonstrating how these powerful models can enhance complex data-driven systems like recommendation engines, which is highly relevant for aiml and r&d roles. research how traditional recommendation systems work, then brainstorm ways an llm could improve them.
why: explores cutting-edge llm use in recommendation systems, vital for aiml/r&d.

title: Every Amazon SaaS claims to use AI
author: claudiuclement
summary: this brief news item points out a common trend: nearly every software-as-a-service (saas) product from amazon now claims to incorporate ai. this observation highlights what's sometimes called "ai washing," where companies heavily market their products using "ai" buzzwords, even if the actual artificial intelligence component is not particularly advanced or central to the product's core function. it's a good reminder for you to develop a critical perspective. when you encounter such claims, try to look beyond the marketing hype and understand what specific ai technologies are actually being used and how they genuinely add value. this critical thinking will be valuable as you evaluate products and potential roles.
why: it highlights the "ai washing" trend, urging critical evaluation of ai claims in product marketing.
